name: PowerHouse

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading:
This Ashburn, Virginia building is now known as CyrusOne NVA14, but its early history belongs to a different company. Public records from PowerHouse Data Centers, a Northern Virginia based data center developer founded in 2021, describe a facility at this location, referred to in the developer's own materials as PowerHouse ABX-1, built on roughly 10 acres with about 265,850 square feet of developable space and up to 60 megawatts of utility power capacity. PowerHouse states the building became fully operational in October 2023 and was sold in the fourth quarter of 2024, which lines up with the property now carrying a CyrusOne name and campus number rather than a PowerHouse one.

PowerHouse itself describes its business as building rather than operating, a real estate developer delivering both shell buildings and fully turnkey data centers for other companies to occupy or acquire, with a portfolio the company says spans roughly 39 million square feet of facilities completed, under construction or planned across nine US markets, representing close to 10 gigawatts of capacity. A build and sell model of that kind is a common pattern in the current data center industry, where developers with land, power interconnection queue positions and construction capacity deliver finished buildings to hyperscale and colocation operators that prefer to acquire operational capacity rather than manage ground up development themselves. Under that reading, PowerHouse ABX-1 was very plausibly built specifically to be sold once complete, with CyrusOne as the buyer that took over operations in late 2024 and folded the building into its own numbering.

CyrusOne is a large, established data center operator with a long standing Northern Virginia campus in nearby Sterling, where its buildings are numbered NVA1 through roughly NVA9. A facility numbered NVA14 sits well beyond that existing sequence, consistent with a building added to the portfolio through an acquisition rather than through CyrusOne's own ground up construction and numbering. Neither company's public materials directly confirm the transaction in a joint statement, so the connection described here rests on the matching address, timeline and sale reference in PowerHouse's own facility page rather than on an announced deal. No updated power, square footage or tenancy figures under CyrusOne's ownership have been published for this specific building since the reported 2024 sale.

profile.reading:
PowerHouse CTP-02 is one of two data center buildings under construction as part of a joint venture between PowerHouse Data Centers and Chirisa Technology Parks on a technology campus in Chesterfield County, Virginia, near Richmond. PowerHouse Data Centers is the data center development division of American Real Estate Partners, a company that describes itself as owning the land under its projects and pursuing fast track utility and permitting approvals. Chirisa Technology Parks, the development platform of Chirisa Investments, brought its existing Richmond area campus, known as CTP, into the partnership.

The CTP campus sits on roughly 230 acres and is master planned for four data center buildings totaling about 534,000 square feet and 360 megawatts of utility power once fully built, according to Chirisa's own published figures. The first building, CTP-01, is already operational, a 250,000 square foot facility drawing 28 megawatts that Chirisa describes as fully leased. CTP-02 and its companion building CTP-03 are the next phase, together accounting for roughly 284,000 square feet and 120 megawatts of reserved utility power, and were listed as under construction as of the most recent published figures. A joint announcement by the two companies named CoreWeave, a cloud provider specializing in GPU compute, as the customer driving the expansion, though the release did not break out which building or buildings CoreWeave's capacity occupies.

The same announcement described a related, adjacent development called Digital Drive on a separate 104 acre site, with three buildings and 300 megawatts fed from Dominion Energy's nearby Meadowville substation, part of a broader plan to bring roughly one gigawatt of capacity to the area over time. PowerHouse and Chirisa said the combined Richmond area buildout was expected to create 800 to 1,200 jobs over five to seven years, with the first buildings targeted for delivery in 2026 and the full campus complete by 2028. PowerHouse's own site lists the entire Richmond market, including CTP-01 through CTP-03 and Digital Drive together, at 320 megawatts.

What neither company publishes is a per building breakdown for CTP-02 alone. There is no public street address, no individual power draw, and no square footage specific to that one structure among the four planned on the CTP campus. The figures available describe CTP-02 and CTP-03 as a pair rather than singly, which is common practice for phased hyperscale campuses where buildings share substations, cooling loops, and site infrastructure rather than standing as fully independent facilities.

sources.title: Chirisa Technology Parks and PowerHouse Data Centers to Launch Next-Generation Hyperscale Campus in Chesterfield County

profile.research_note: PowerHouse and Chirisa's joint CTP-02/CTP-03 development in Chesterfield County VA (for CoreWeave) is confirmed real via press release, but no source found (PowerHouse site, PR Newswire, or trade press) publishes an exact street address or per-building MW/sqft figure for CTP-02 specifically -- only the combined CTP-02+CTP-03 320MW figure noted earlier.

reading:
PowerHouse Data Centers was founded in 2021 and is redeveloping the former AOL headquarters site in Sterling, Virginia, per Data Center Dynamics reporting on demolition work there, which this entry treats as the operator's likely home base given its status as the company's primary named market. The operator's own homepage does not state a precise headquarters address or ownership structure.

The company describes an unusually large forward pipeline, 140 data centers underway or in planning across nine major US market regions, spanning Northern Virginia, Richmond and Spotsylvania in Virginia, Irving, Grand Prairie, and Red Oak in Texas, Carlisle, Pennsylvania, Charlotte, North Carolina, Reno, Nevada, three Indiana markets, Joliet, Illinois, and Louisville, Kentucky. PowerHouse states nearly 10 gigawatts of total capacity across these planned and underway facilities, with individual markets ranging from 150 megawatts to 1.8 gigawatts, and positions itself specifically around high performance computing, high density power, and immersive cooling solutions.

The registry here tracks 2 PowerHouse facilities, both in Virginia. PowerHouse's stated nearly 10 gigawatt pipeline is, by a wide margin, the largest forward capacity figure recorded across any operator in this registry so far, exceeding Aligned's 6.4 gigawatts and CloudHQ's 6,000-plus megawatt expansion potential, though as a 2021-founded company with facilities described as underway or in planning rather than operating, these figures describe pipeline ambition rather than built and energized capacity.

sources.title: Data Center Dynamics, PowerHouse begins demolition work on former AOL HQ in Sterling, Virginia
